svg.title: How charter's ideas fit (charter 0.4.19)
svg.desc: Twenty-five concepts in six clusters: who acts, the written charter, the unit of work, the gates, running the road, and what is true. Lines carry a verb; their style says who acts: thick teal the owner, navy a citation, dashed grey a proposal, indigo a gate, dotted violet a machine record.
svg.text: WHAT IS TRUE, AND WHAT IT COST

g.title: Unit: One deliverable as a tasket: cites a scope item or a rail, declares a perimeter, lists acceptance, carries evidence and a log. One session owns it.
g.text: names an item of the road

g.title: Perimeter: The paths a unit may touch. A file outside it needs a - path: why line under ## Outside perimeter before the commit.
g.text: the paths it may touch; outside needs a note

g.title: Acceptance: Checkbox lines, one binary probe each. (guard) marks one that protects behaviour that already works; — owner: one that only the owner may close.
Evidence: A commit SHA that resolves, a path:line, and the $ command lines of the probes. A path or a URL alone is refused.
Log: Dated lines appended when something lands or the session stops. A resumed session reads the unit, not the transcript.
g.text: a new session resumes from here

g.title: Probe: The command that answers one criterion yes or no. It fails before the work and passes after; with an opt-in the gates run it again, also at the unit's base.
Accepted: Done means accepted: every box checked and evidence that resolves. A done flip without it is refused; the synthesis lists done and accepted apart from the rest.
g.text: else refused, in session and at commit

g.title: Owner: The person who signs and rules: approves change requests, rules decisions, commits owner-only changes and merges. Named in owner in charter/config.json for the CI author check.
Agent session: Works one unit at a time and is its single writer. Proposes what it cannot settle: a change request, a decision, a hand-over.
Owner's delegate: Takes owner acts up to the level the owner set (strict, routine, answers, open), after rules and a model judge them. Structural changes are never delegated.
Track: client when a signed devis covers the project, prototype otherwise. It selects which gates are hard: the scope gate runs only on the client track.
Scope: The summary of the signed devis: what is sold, what is not, what is assumed. Client track only; the owner's file.
Change request: Work outside the scope. Anyone proposes it; its paths stay refused until the owner sets approved, approved_by and approved_on.
Rails: The road, items in order. Every open unit names one; adding an item is the recorded re-plan; a chain group is one item.
Decision: One choice with ## Because and expires:. Code cites it as charter:<id>; its check: runs on files its binds: names. A project lesson is a decision with kind: lesson.

Owner-only keys: The files and fields that define the gates: scope, rails, config, the engine, settings, the CI workflow, approval and ruling fields, split units, — owner: lines. Refused to an agent's edit.
Gate: A check that refuses (hard) or warns. Hard: scope, size, done, decisions in their retired and failing forms, anchors in CI, owner-only changes. The rest warns and is logged.
Three lines: Where the same gate runs: in the session (Claude Code hooks), at commit (git pre-commit, any agent), at merge (CI from a clean clone). Each catches what the one before can miss.
Override: The honest way past a refusal, named in it: write the change request, move code out of a frozen file, add the evidence, propose a successor decision.
g.text: the code out · add the evidence ·

g.title: Gate log: Every finding with its gate, level and path; per machine, never committed. A warning that keeps firing on real problems is the case for making it a gate.

Chain: Fresh sessions over the road: rules injected verbatim, hand over at 25% of the context window (past 30% only the handoff, unit files, git and the charter CLI pass), a validated handoff, a review per group, waits on the owner with owner.md.
Independent reviewer: A party that wrote neither side: reviews each group of a chain, reviews the owner's acts at a wait, and signs the review: evidence line when review.required is on.
Anchor: What a claim points at. Four evidence classes: measured (resolves here), vendor (a URL), reported and inference (admitted, counted apart).
Progress synthesis: Generated by charter synth from the repository, never edited by hand; refuses to write when its own anchor check fails.
Ledger: Tokens and estimated cost per session, folded per unit; cost per accepted unit, printed as a lower bound while any cost is unknown.

g.text: commits some owner acts, by level
charges each session to the unit
